title: Lascaux and Chauvet
objective: After this level you can describe the animal paintings in the caves of Lascaux and Chauvet.
summary: Lascaux (about 17,000 years old) has huge black aurochs and closed in 1963 after visitors harmed it. Chauvet (about 35,500 years old) is full of lions, rhinos and mammoths.

cards.headline: In 1994, cave explorers in France felt a faint draft from a pile of stones.
cards.body: Behind it was a cave sealed by rockfalls for at least 21,000 years. On its walls: cave lions, woolly rhinos and mammoths. But first, meet an older discovery: Lascaux.

cards.headline: Lascaux: the Hall of the Bulls
cards.body: Four teenagers found Lascaux in 1940. Radiocarbon dating of its charcoal says about 17,000 years old. In its most famous room, four huge black bulls (aurochs) sweep across the rock, some about 5 meters long. Their bodies are drawn from the side, but their horns twist toward you, so you see both at once. The painters built scaffolding to reach the ceiling.

cards.fact: Lascaux lasted about 17,000 years in the dark, then about 15 years of tourists.
cards.context: It opened to visitors in 1948, up to 100,000 a year. Their traffic and the artificial lights faded the colors and brought algae, bacteria and crystals. In 1963 it closed. Since 1983, visitors have toured a replica nearby instead.

mascot.line: Sometimes the kindest way to love a painting is to stop breathing on it.

cards.headline: Chauvet: twice as old
cards.body: Radiocarbon dates put most of Chauvet's art at about 35,500 years old, roughly twice Lascaux's age. Its artists chose dangerous animals: among over 400 animals of 14 species are cave lions, woolly rhinos, mammoths and bears. They scraped walls clean, strengthened outlines and smudged charcoal to shade. In the End Chamber, a pride of lions hunts bison.

cards.headline: Two great caves: explored
learned: Its Hall of the Bulls holds four huge aurochs
Visitors damaged it; it closed in 1963
Chauvet: about 35,500 years old, full of dangerous animals

questions.prompt: What fills Lascaux's most famous room, the Hall of the Bulls?

options.label: Lions hunting bison
options.rationale: That scene is in Chauvet's End Chamber.

options.label: Rows of hand stencils
options.rationale: Lascaux is famous for its animals.

questions.explanation: Four huge black bulls, or aurochs, some about 5 meters long, with horns twisted to face you.

questions.prompt: Why was Lascaux closed to the public in 1963?

options.label: A rockfall blocked the cave's entrance
options.rationale: That happened to Chauvet, long ago.

options.label: Visitors and lights were damaging the paintings
The paintings were found to be fakes
Heavy rain flooded the lower chambers
options.rationale: Water wasn't the problem; people were.

questions.explanation: Up to 100,000 visitors a year and artificial lighting faded the colors and brought algae, bacteria and crystals.

questions.prompt: Chauvet's artists smudged charcoal to shade their animals. Which Level 3 element does shading help create?

options.label: Line, the outline of each animal
options.rationale: The outlines are line; the shading does something else.

options.label: Negative space around the animals
options.rationale: That's the empty area around a shape.

options.label: Geometric shape, like circles
options.rationale: The animals are organic, not squares and circles.

questions.explanation: Shading makes the animals look rounded and solid, giving a flat wall the feeling of depth: space.
